free_tier.stated: Zero bytes. NIP-94 is a metadata event: `url`, `m` (mime), `size`, `dim`, `i` (torrent infohash), `thumb`. The relay stores the JSON pointer, the file lives elsewhere.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap = relay event size limit (~64 KB

retention.stated: until the instance is recycled; not persistent

egress.terms: N/a. Relay never serves the file.

record.tooling: nostr websocket protocol (EVENT/REQ), `nak` CLI. Relays are free and accept arbitrary events, but the event size limit (typ. 64 KB) caps any inline-base64 trick at ~48 KB.
record.chaining: Chains with Blossom: NIP-94/NIP-96 events make Blossom blobs discoverable and re-mirrorable. On its own this is not storage.

limits.value: per-object-cap = relay event size limit (~64 KB

record.limits_note: per-object-cap: Bounded by relay event size limits (~64 KB typical). Base64 encoding overhead leaves approximately 48 KB of payload data per event.
record.reliability_note: Relays are ephemeral and freely delete events; free relays exist in the thousands but none is a byte store.

evidence.proved: tags are `url`, `m`, `size`, `dim`, `i` (torrent infohash), `thumb`; 'A relay for indexing shared files. For example, to promote torrents.' — confirms metadata-only semantics
